page.title: Downloads
page.description: Download the sanitised snapshot of the Webconsulting TYPO3 Lab: the database, the Fileadmin archive and a script that installs both in DDEV.

content.bodytext:
This is a complete copy of the lab. You get the database, the matching Fileadmin archive and a script that sets both up in a DDEV site.

Downloads

  • install.txt — setup script, run it with bash install.txt (3 KB)
  • db-public.zip — database, sanitised (14 MB)
  • fileadmin-public.zip — matching Fileadmin contents (325 MB)
  • snapshot-readme.txt — what is in the snapshot

Quick start

You need Docker or OrbStack, DDEV 1.25.3 or newer, and Git. The downloads ask for the same credentials you used to reach this page.

curl -fLO https://typo3-lab.webconsulting.at/fileadmin/_downloads/install.txt
bash install.txt

The script clones the repository, fetches both archives and runs the documented bootstrap. Sign in at /typo3/ with admin / Demo123*, then change that password.

The .txt and .zip extensions are deliberate. TYPO3 denies access to .sh and .sql files in the document root, and that rule should stay. The archives are zip files, not .tar.gz, because Apache serves any .gz file with Content-Encoding: gzip. Browsers then decode it without telling you. You would save a file named .tar.gz that is really a plain tar, and the import would reject it.

What “sanitised” means

The published database is not the one this site runs on. Tables with credentials or personal data keep their structure but ship with no rows:

  • Vault secrets
  • API and MCP access tokens
  • OAuth records
  • WorkOS identities
  • the LLM provider credential
  • every backend and frontend account
  • form submissions and blog comments
  • the log and history tables
  • visitor data: search statistics with IP addresses, browser reports, preview links and sessions
  • LLM and agent runs with their usage and telemetry

One demo administrator is added in their place.

Integrations that need credentials therefore start switched off. Add your own keys as described in After the import below.

Import the database and the Fileadmin archive together. The database references files by uid, so a mismatched pair shows broken images.

After the import: what you add

The lab runs without a single key. The features below stay off until you add yours. Do the first two steps in every case; the rest only for the features you want. After changing an environment variable, run ddev restart.

  1. Change the admin password. Sign in at /typo3/ with admin / Demo123*, open your user settings and set a new password.

  2. Build the search index. Solr runs inside DDEV and needs no key:

    ddev exec vendor/bin/typo3 sitepackage:solr:reindex --index

  3. AI features (AI assistant, nr-llm examples, image generation, Agent Nexus, Skillflow runs). Create an API key at platform.openai.com. In the backend open AI → LLM Setup, edit the OpenAI provider and enter the key; nr-llm keeps it in the Vault. Then let the lab copy the key reference into the image service:

    ddev exec vendor/bin/typo3 sitepackage:configure-ai-examples

  4. Jev form decisions (the Powermail forms that route by content). Create a TypeSafe API key, then open Admin Tools → Vault and add a secret with the identifier typesafe_api_key.

  5. Spam protection on forms (Friendly Captcha). Create a site at friendlycaptcha.com and set its two keys as environment variables, for DDEV in .ddev/config.local.yaml under web_environment: FRIENDLYCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY and FRIENDLYCAPTCHA_API_KEY. The free plan is for non-commercial use.

  6. Login with WorkOS (the login demos under Features). Copy the API key and the client ID from the WorkOS dashboard into TYPO3_WORKOS_API_KEY and TYPO3_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID, and add your site’s callback URL in WorkOS.

  7. MCP server (Claude, Cursor and other agents). All access tokens were removed. Create a new one for each client in the backend’s MCP module and paste it into the client’s MCP configuration.

  8. Slack bridge (optional). Set WEBCON_MCP_CHAT_BRIDGE_API_TOKEN, WEBCON_MCP_CHAT_BRIDGE_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, WEBCON_MCP_CHAT_BRIDGE_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET and WEBCON_MCP_CHAT_BRIDGE_SLACK_WEBHOOK from your Slack app.

  9. Paywall demo (x402, optional). It runs on the Base Sepolia test network with a placeholder wallet. To receive test payments, put your own wallet address into config/sites/blog/config.yaml under x402_paywall.wallet_address.

  10. Email. DDEV catches every message in Mailpit (ddev launch -m), so forms work without setup. For real delivery set TYPO3_MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp and TYPO3_MAIL_SMTP_SERVER, TYPO3_MAIL_SMTP_USERNAME, TYPO3_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD.

  11. For developers only: the Flue integration reads an Anthropic key from the Vault secret flue_anthropic_api_key, and regenerating the product film’s narration and music needs a FAL_KEY from fal.ai (Build/Scripts/generate-film-audio.mjs).

Keys never go into the database dump or the repository: environment variables stay on your machine, and the Vault encrypts what it stores.
